prespecified_units.measure: Vaccine Efficacy (VE) of Two Doses of Tetravalent Dengue Vaccine Candidate (TDV) in Preventing Virologically-Confirmed Dengue Fever Induced by Any Dengue Serotype
prespecified_units.timeframe: From 30 days post-second vaccination (Day 120) until the end of Part 1 (120 cases of dengue fever are confirmed and minimum duration of subject follow-up of 12 months post-second vaccination)
prespecified_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
prespecified_units.result_quote: VE against VCD across serotypes was 43.5% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 25.3%, 57.3%) for 4-5 year-olds; 63.5% (95% CI: 56.9%, 69.1%) for 6-11 year-olds, and 67.7% (95% CI: 57.8%, 75.2%) for 12-16 year-olds.

prespecified_units.measure: VE of Two Doses of TDV in Preventing Hospitalization due to Virologically-Confirmed Dengue Fever Induced by Any Dengue Serotype
prespecified_units.timeframe: From 30 days post-second vaccination (Day 120) until the end of Part 2 (21 months)
prespecified_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
prespecified_units.result_quote: VE against hospitalized VCD was 63.8% (95% CI: 21.1%, 83.4%), 85.1% (95% CI: 77.1%, 90.3%), and 89.7% (95% CI: 77.9%, 95.2%), for the 3 age groups, respectively.

prespecified_units.role_evidence_quote: Solicited and unsolicited AEs, SAEs, AEs leading to study discontinuation, SAEs related to the investigational product, and deaths during the study are reported for each age group.

additional_units.reported_label: two episodes of symptomatic dengue
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: Herein, we describe these multiple episodes of symptomatic dengue, together with an exploratory estimate of the effect of vaccination on subsequent dengue episodes.
additional_units.result_quote: 5 of 13,380 TAK-003 recipients and 13 of 6,687 placebo recipients experienced two episodes of symptomatic dengue between the first dose and the end of the study,  57 months later (patients received the second dose 3 months after the first dose).

additional_units.reported_label: homotypic reinfection
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: Herein, we describe these multiple episodes of symptomatic dengue, together with an exploratory estimate of the effect of vaccination on subsequent dengue episodes.
additional_units.result_quote: Two of these participants experienced repeat infection with the same serotype (i.e., homotypic reinfection).

additional_units.reported_label: relative risk of a subsequent episode of symptomatic dengue
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: Herein, we describe these multiple episodes of symptomatic dengue, together with an exploratory estimate of the effect of vaccination on subsequent dengue episodes.
additional_units.result_quote: In comparison with placebo, the relative risk of a subsequent episode of symptomatic dengue was 0.19 (95% CI, 0.07-0.54) in TAK-003 recipients.

additional_units.reported_label: at least one VCD episode
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: In  57 months after the first dose, 442 participants (3.3%) in the TAK-003 group and 547 (8.2%) in the placebo group experienced at least one VCD episode ( Table 1 ).

additional_units.reported_label: two VCD episodes
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Five participants (0.04%) in the TAK-003 group and 13 (0.19%) in the placebo group experienced two VCD episodes during this time frame, resulting in a relative risk of the subsequent VCD episode versus placebo of 0.19 (95% CI, 0.07-0.54) based on the safety set, and 0.48 (95% CI, 0.17-1.32) based on the population of participants who had experienced at least one VCD episode.

additional_units.reported_label: sequential episodes of VCD at trial sites
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Ten of the sequential episodes of VCD occurred at the sites in the Philippines, four in Colombia, three in Sri Lanka, and one in Thailand ( Table 2 ).

additional_units.reported_label: time interval between first and subsequent VCD episode
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Subsequent episodes occurred 46 to 1,181 days after the first episode recorded in the trial (mean, 500 days).

additional_units.reported_label: serotype of subsequent VCD episodes
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Of the subsequent episodes, five were DENV-1, seven were DENV-2, three were DENV-3, and three were DENV-4.

additional_units.reported_label: homotypic VCD
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: There were two instances of homotypic VCD: one DENV-3 case occurring 763 days after the first episode in a male participant from the Philippines who was 12 years old at enrollment and seropositive at baseline, and one DENV-1 case occurring 207 days after the first episode in a 7-year-old seronegative female participant from Colombia.

additional_units.reported_label: first episodes diagnosed clinically as dengue by the investigators
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: In the 18 participants who experienced two VCD episodes, five of the first episodes after trial vaccination were diagnosed clinically as dengue by the investigators, and three participants were hospitalized (one episode each of DENV-1, -2, and -3).

additional_units.reported_label: hospitalization during first VCD episodes
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: In the 18 participants who experienced two VCD episodes, five of the first episodes after trial vaccination were diagnosed clinically as dengue by the investigators, and three participants were hospitalized (one episode each of DENV-1, -2, and -3).

additional_units.reported_label: subsequent episodes diagnosed clinically as dengue
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Two of the subsequent episodes (DENV-1 homotypic reinfection and DENV-4 following DENV-2) were diagnosed clinically as dengue and both required hospitalization.

additional_units.reported_label: hospitalization during subsequent VCD episodes
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Two of the subsequent episodes (DENV-1 homotypic reinfection and DENV-4 following DENV-2) were diagnosed clinically as dengue and both required hospitalization.

additional_units.reported_label: severity classification by the adjudication committee
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: One of the first VCD episodes (DENV-3 in a baseline seronegative participant) was classified as severe by the adjudication committee; none of the other episodes were classified as severe or dengue hemorrhagic fever.

additional_units.reported_label: dengue hemorrhagic fever
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: One of the first VCD episodes (DENV-3 in a baseline seronegative participant) was classified as severe by the adjudication committee; none of the other episodes were classified as severe or dengue hemorrhagic fever.

additional_units.reported_label: distribution by vaccination group among participants with two VCD episodes
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Although this is a small number of cases, the distribution by vaccination group (five in the TAK-003 group versus 13 in the placebo group; 2:1 randomization ratio) provides some evidence of the lower risk of a subsequent symptomatic dengue episode in people who have postvaccination breakthrough cases.

additional_units.reported_label: serotype distribution of first episodes among participants with two VCD episodes
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Among the 18 sequential episodes, the majority of the cases (i.e., 13 of 18 first episodes and 12 of 18 subsequent episodes) were caused by DENV-1 or -2.

additional_units.reported_label: serotype distribution of subsequent episodes among participants with two VCD episodes
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Among the 18 sequential episodes, the majority of the cases (i.e., 13 of 18 first episodes and 12 of 18 subsequent episodes) were caused by DENV-1 or -2.

additional_units.reported_label: DENV-1 and DENV-2 cases in the placebo group
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: This reflects the data in the placebo group over  57 months in eight dengue-endemic countries, in which these two serotypes accounted for the majority of dengue cases (423 of 560).

additional_units.reported_label: cases of homotypic reinfection
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: All the analyses presented in this manuscript are exploratory and post hoc in nature.
additional_units.result_quote: Notably, we observed no clear patterns in causative serotype of sequential episodes, but we did record two cases of homotypic reinfection.

additional_units.role_evidence_quote: Evaluation of the impact of prior JE or YF vaccination on VE, safety, and immunogenicity was exploratory and included both prespecified and post hoc analyses.

additional_units.reported_label: study completion through the end of Part 3
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: Participants (or their parents/guardians) were contacted at least weekly to monitor for febrile illness and potential dengue cases.
additional_units.result_quote: Overall, 94.2% of 4-5 year-olds, 93.9% of 6-11 year-olds, and 84.7% of 12-16 year-olds completed the study through the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination; median duration of follow-up after the second dose was 1641 days).

additional_units.reported_label: VCD cases
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: Across age groups, 560 cases of VCD were recorded from first vaccination to end of Part 3 in the placebo group, and 447 in the TAK-003 group.

additional_units.reported_label: causative serotype of VCD cases in placebo recipients
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: The predominant causative serotype in placebo recipients varied by age, with DENV-1 and DENV-3 causing the most cases in 4-5 year-olds (33.3% and 35.4%, respectively) compared with DENV-1 and DENV-2 in children aged >=6 years (6-11 year-olds-DENV-1: 42.2%; DENV-2: 36.7%; 12-16 year-olds-DENV-1: 43.8%; DENV-2: 35.0%; Figure 1 A ).

additional_units.reported_label: causative serotype of hospitalized VCD cases in placebo recipients
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: DENV-1 and DENV-2 caused the majority of hospitalized cases across age groups (66.7%-89.5%), whereas DENV-3 caused proportionally more hospitalized cases in 4-5 year-olds than in older children ( Figure 1 B ).

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD by age group
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: Across serotypes and baseline serostatus, VE against VCD ranged from 43.5% (95% CI: 25.3%, 57.3%) in 4-5 year-olds through to 67.7% (95% CI: 57.8%, 75.2%) in 12-16 year-olds ( Figure 2 A ).

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD in seropositive 6-11 year-olds
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: in 6-11 year-olds VE was 64.8% (95% CI: 57.0%, 71.2%) in seropositive and 60.5% (95% CI: 46.8%, 70.7%) in seronegative participants

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD in seronegative 6-11 year-olds
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: in 6-11 year-olds VE was 64.8% (95% CI: 57.0%, 71.2%) in seropositive and 60.5% (95% CI: 46.8%, 70.7%) in seronegative participants

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD in seropositive 12-16 year-olds
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: in 12-16 year-olds these were 68.6% (95% CI: 57.7%, 76.7%) and 63.6% (95% CI: 33.8%, 79.9%), respectively.

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD in seronegative 12-16 year-olds
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: in 12-16 year-olds these were 68.6% (95% CI: 57.7%, 76.7%) and 63.6% (95% CI: 33.8%, 79.9%), respectively.

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD in seropositive 4-5 year-olds
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: VE in 4-5 year-olds was 54.1% (95% CI: 34.1%, 68.0%) in seropositive and 23.2% (95% CI: -20.0%, 50.8%) in seronegative participants.

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD in seronegative 4-5 year-olds
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: VE in 4-5 year-olds was 54.1% (95% CI: 34.1%, 68.0%) in seropositive and 23.2% (95% CI: -20.0%, 50.8%) in seronegative participants.

additional_units.reported_label: VE against hospitalized VCD by age group
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: Across baseline serostatuses, VE against hospitalized VCD was 63.8% (95% CI: 21.1%, 83.4%) in the 4-5 year-olds, 85.1% (95% CI: 77.1%, 90.3%) in 6-11 year-olds, and 89.7% (95% CI: 77.9%, 95.2%) in 12-16 year-olds.

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD by year of age in seropositive participants
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: Estimates of VE of TAK-003 against VCD by year of age ranged from 49.1% (95% CI: 18.8%, 68.0%) in 9 year-olds to 76.9% (95% CI: 26.1%, 92.8%) in 16 year-olds in seropositive participants ( Supplementary Table 2 ).

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD by year of age in seronegative participants
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: More variation was seen in seronegative participants, ranging from -30.2% (-1152.1%, 86.5%) in 15 year-olds to 92.7% (95% CI: 67.4%, 98.3%) in 12 year-olds, with very few cases in children >12 years of age.

additional_units.reported_label: VE against hospitalized VCD in seropositive participants by year of age
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: VE against hospitalized VCD was generally >75% across age groups in seropositive participants, with the exception of 4 year-olds (VE 3.1%, 95% CI: -287.4%, 75.8%) and 16 year-olds (68.0%, 95% CI: -252.9%, 97.1%).

additional_units.reported_label: VE against hospitalized VCD in seronegative participants by year of age
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: In seronegative participants, VE ranged from 51.3% to 100% in children aged 4-12 years, although was associated with large confidence intervals, and no cases reported in older children ( Supplementary Table 3 ).

additional_units.reported_label: VE against VCD by individual study year
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: This pre-specified exploratory analysis evaluates the VE of TAK-003 in preventing VCD and hospitalized VCD from first dose to the end of Part 3 (approximately 57 months postvaccination) stratified by year of age and age group (4-5 years, 6-11 years, or 12-16 years) at enrolment.
additional_units.result_quote: Evaluation of VE against VCD by individual study year showed substantial year-by-year variation in 4-5 year-olds and seronegative 12-16 year-olds ( Supplementary Table 4 ).

additional_units.reported_label: severe dengue cases
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: Clinical Signs and Symptoms of VCD by Age Group and Baseline Serostatus
additional_units.result_quote: In total, 3 severe dengue cases were reported in 4-5 year-olds (1 seronegative, 2 seropositive), 5 in 6-11 year-olds (1 seronegative, 4 seropositive), and 0 in 12-16 year-olds.

additional_units.reported_label: DHF cases
additional_units.role_evidence_quote: Clinical Signs and Symptoms of VCD by Age Group and Baseline Serostatus
additional_units.result_quote: In total, 4 cases of DHF were reported in 4-5 year-olds, 10 in 6-11 year-olds, and 10 in 12-16 year-olds, with the majority of cases in baseline seropositive placebo recipients ( Supplementary Table 9 ).
